records.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: corrected transparent pixel-art tactical game unit for MIDDLE-EARTH WARBANDS.
Image 1 is the AUTHORITATIVE ORIGINAL character identity, equipment, colors and dynamic pose to redraw. Image 2 is only the approved PIXEL STYLE / elevated camera reference, not an outfit, silhouette or body-size template.
Restore the ORIGINAL identity and action instead of inventing a redesign. Keep exact armor shapes, helmet/hood, face visibility, hair, cape, weapons and meaningful emblems from image 1. No ornate additions. Preserve torso lean, arm gestures, weapon diagonal, forward step and flowing silhouette; never standardize everyone into the same wide-legged upright guard pose.
CAMERA: elevated FRONT view looking down 30–40 degrees, showing crown and both shoulder TOPS, chest foreshortening and top surfaces of the feet. Keep original front-facing action with slight diagonal, not eye-level frontal, not side view, not vertical overhead. Head naturally bowed, chin down, gaze toward forward-ground; hair/helmet brow shadows the eyes. Raising camera is separate from bowing the head.
ANATOMY: human/elf adult standing anatomy exactly FIVE anatomical heads tall, crown-to-chin unit excludes hair and helmet decorations. Cohesive shoulders, arms, hands, pelvis, naturally bent knees and ankles, moderate stance width, useful leg length. Not chibi four-head body, not elongated six-to-eight-head adult. For orcs, hobbits, wraiths, trolls and animals retain the source's SPECIES proportions, not human anatomy. Do not shrink the head alone.
STYLE: deliberately clustered crisp PIXEL ART, stepped dark outlines, matching image 2's pixel density, restrained colors and top-left lighting. Avoid glossy smooth illustration, 3D or airbrushed detail. Preserve readable material planes.
One complete isolated unit, actual transparent alpha, NO base, ground shadow, scenery, lettering or extra objects. All weapon tips, cape edges and feet fully inside canvas with at least 4% clear transparent margin. Center on BODY, not weapon. Finish all connected limbs and weapon grips cleanly.

Recreate the original equipment and dynamic silhouette faithfully; avoid excessive decorative gold and preserve anatomical leg length with a moderate stance.
